title: FARCRAFT - Chant The Dead - Where do you draw the line on AI?
author: Riitoken

comments.author: Aineisa
comments.body:
Who set the line? Is it just arbitrarily placed?

As a solo dev with a near $0 budget im going to use whatever tools at my disposal to create the best I can do. 

Currently thật means a mix of AI and manual work to fix its mistakes. 

I don’t get all this hand wringing and wailing about no longer having to do mundane work like set up third person controls to the common standard gamers expect or even doing complex stuff like procedural generation. 

Anyway. Get the best version of your idea thật you can get. If that means doing it all by yourself then great.

replies.author: Riitoken
replies.body: I like the way you think.

replies.author: IndubitablyNerdy
replies.body:
Agree, on top of that I might add that when a tiny studio use this tool they are not actually subtracting labor for anyone as without this technology that project will simply not exist. 

It is not a choice between a solo dev using AI and hiring an artist, because the second half would never happen due to budget (and to the fact that a lot of indie projects are just done uniquely for the developer own enjoyment, often there isn't even any commercial return).

Now when a corporate titan that actually has the means to pay people fairly does it though it is differnet for me.

The problem with AI I think lies in this, the technology into itself is extremely useful, but who owns the benefits (a tiny minority of shareholders, or society as a whole) should be central to any discussion as with any technology that strongly devalue labor versus capital.

replies.author: Aineisa
replies.body:
Where was this discussion when automation took over factory jobs? Should society go back to using horses because then we need to bring back the horse poop scooping jobs? 

You could easily slap your last argument onto those situations “who owns the benefits of the automobile. Shareholders or society.”

Every new technology disrupts. Every new technology brings changes to wealth. 

Oil made a lot of poor people rich. From the poor farmer who owned oil rich land to the automobile maker and down to the mechanics who created whole businesses services autos. 

New technology results in new work. 

For those who are passionate about telling stories or having unique game mechanics AI takes out a lot of the mundane tasks like coding standard game mechanics or tree and grass meshes and I think as a result there will be a lot more creative jobs opening up. 

Naturally I expect you’ll reply with some worry about “slop” however slop has always existed and society has always managed to find what society wants. Take YouTube for example.
